title: Findings ledger event (v1)
description: One JSON object per line of an append-only, repo-local ledger (default `.style-findings.jsonl` at the main worktree root). Four event kinds share the file: `finding` (something was flagged), `outcome` (what became of it), `gate_pass` (an automated gate passed over these files), `review_run` (one review round of a change happened; it counts toward the round cap and does not change any finding). The current state of a finding is the fold of its events in file order: it is open until an `outcome` for its id appears; a later `finding` with the same id after an outcome re-opens it (gate source only; l1/l2 re-adds are ignored). `rule_id` is one of: a clause id defined in the repo's configured rules files, `unmapped`, or `<tool>:<code>` (for example `ruff:F811`). This schema only checks the shape of a rule id; whether a clause exists is checked against the rules files when an event is written, not when old events are read. IDs: l1/l2 -> `<repo>:<source>:<run_id>:<display_id>`; gate -> `<repo>:gate:<sha1 of file|rule_code|whitespace-stripped line text, first 12 hex>`, so repeats of one issue fold into one finding (gate events carry run_id `gate` and a display_id equal to the 12-hex hash). `ts` is local time without a timezone. Fields added after the first v1 ledgers (`discovered_at`, `also_matches`, `rule_id_source`, `snippet_source`, and on `review_run` `reviewer`, `reviewer_version`, `level`, `head`, `version_changed`, `tree`, `trigger`) are optional, the `review_run` kind is additive, and every line of an older v1 ledger still validates.

rule_id.description: A clause id from the configured rules files (for example P0E.2, R.7), `unmapped`, or `<tool>:<code>` (for example ruff:F811).

display_id.description: Short handle for humans; the value to put in a `Fixes-Finding:` commit trailer.

ts.description: When the event was written to the ledger.

rule_code.description: What the detector called it: a tool code, a gate code, or the category text a reviewer gave.

category.description: Free-form grouping label. Older ledgers use a fixed set (exception, fallback, complexity, ...); new events carry the clause family (P0E), the tool name (ruff) or `unmapped`.

snippet.description: Optional code context captured when the finding was recorded. `ratchet review` fills it with the flagged line and up to three lines either side (at most 7 lines and about 600 characters); a snippet that is less than that window ends with the line `[snippet truncated]`. `add` records the text it is given and `ingest-code-review` records none.

snippet_source.description: Optional; written by `ratchet review` only. Where the snippet was read from: `review` (the code the reviewer read when it started: the files from its saved evidence, or for a file unchanged since HEAD the version in the commit HEAD pointed at then; for a review of a commit range, the files the range changed and any other file, all read from the commit HEAD pointed at then, so uncommitted edits are not in them), `worktree` (the working tree when a --from-file review was imported, which may differ from what the reviewer saw), or `unavailable` (no snippet: the file or line does not exist, the file is outside the repo or unreadable, the review did not capture it, or it was a --target review whose evidence is not verified against the target). Absent on events that did not come from `ratchet review`.

discovered_at.description: Optional. When the reviewer produced the finding, if that differs from `ts` (the ledger write time).

also_matches.description: Optional. Other findings on the same file and line that were collapsed into this one (this event is the most severe).

rule_id_source.description: Optional. Where the rule_id came from: `model` (the category a reviewing model gave, or its lack of one when nothing could be read from its text: then rule_id is unmapped), `human`, `tool` (a tool code, possibly mapped through tool_rule_map), or `attributed` (the model gave no category and the clause id was read out of its summary or failure scenario). Absent on older events.

run.description: The review's run id (the prefix of its findings' display_ids).

round_key.description: Names the change under review: `target:<T>` for a --target, else `<branch>@<first 12 hex of the fork point from the default branch>` (`<branch>@unborn` before the first commit). Rounds are counted per key.

round.description: 1 + the review_run events with this round_key written before this one.

max_rounds.description: The max_review_rounds in force when the review ran.

over_cap.description: True when round > max_rounds, which only a run with --over-cap gets to.

finding_count.description: Findings the review contained, whether or not they were new to the ledger.

reviewer.description: Optional. What ran the review: `claude-code` when `ratchet review` ran it, null for a --from-file review (its reviewer is not known). Absent on older events.

reviewer_version.description: Optional. The stripped stdout of `claude --version`, asked once before the review started; null when the review was read with --from-file or the version could not be read (the run then says so on stderr). Absent on older events.

level.description: Optional. The review level the run used (`low` .. `max`); null for a --from-file review. Absent on older events.

head.description: Optional. The full sha of the commit HEAD pointed at before the reviewer started (for a --from-file review, when the file was read), or `none` on a branch with no commit. Uncommitted changes are not part of it. Absent on older events.

version_changed.description: Optional; written only when true: `reviewer_version` differs from the latest earlier review_run that has one, so this is the first review on the new version.

tree.description: Optional. The id of a git tree holding the worktree as the review found it when it started (for a --from-file review, when the file was read): tracked files as they were on disk, uncommitted work included, and the untracked files git does not ignore. A range review on the default branch reads only commits, so its tree is the tree of the HEAD the range ends at, without uncommitted work. It is how a later wrap-up tells what changed since, whether or not the reviewed work was committed in between. Nothing refers to the tree, so `git gc` may remove it; a reader treats a missing tree object as absent. Absent on older events, for a --target review (no wrap-up measures from one), and when taking the tree failed.

trigger.description: Optional; written only by `ratchet wrapup --auto`, with the value `auto`: the automatic wrap-up, which the Stop hook asks for and a script may too. A record only: the daily cap (config `wrapup_auto_max_per_day`) does not read the ledger, it counts the slots of its own book, `.ratchet/auto-reservations.jsonl`; a reader takes only `auto` as meaningful and ignores any other value. Absent on a review run by `ratchet review` or by `ratchet wrapup` without `--auto`, and on older events.
